sampling_model.design: For each analyst-selected \(s\), the assignment law is chosen from all outcome-independent probability distributions on \(\{0,1\}^{2J}\); after pair-preserving symmetrization it is represented by \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\).
sampling_model.units: The \(2J\) labelled units and all binary potential outcomes are fixed; only the partition into \(J\) pairs is observed before assignment, while armwise discordance is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: A binary assignment \(A\) is the only source of randomness, and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}=A_{jr}Y_{jr}(1)+(1-A_{jr})Y_{jr}(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No marginal positivity restriction is imposed; zero-mass assignment and observation cells are handled by closed quadratic perspectives and explicit primal completions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no sampled nuisances. Nature chooses a fixed schedule in the sensitivity class \(\Theta_{J,s}\); risks, optimal procedures, and confidence sets are reported separately as \(s\) varies.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Given an assignment vector and an invariant estimator, uniform randomization over the permutation group is minimax under invariant states and a quasiconvex objective.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes worst-case variance of difference in means over a structured conditional-mean class and may require randomization over several partitions.
For unrestricted binary potential outcomes, Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear posterior-mean rule attains the all-procedure minimax risk, whose second-order term is governed by the Airy function.

For unrestricted bounded-interval potential outcomes, independent assignment with a nonlinear estimator is minimax; the present unrestricted binary endpoint is only the endpoint-valued subclass, and its same value and procedure transfer through an endpoint-prior lower bound and a uniform upper-bound sandwich.

Within superpopulation stratified designs treating half of every stratum, matched pairs formed by the prognostic index minimize the mean-squared error of difference in means; that problem and the present fixed-population latent-discordance design class are non-nested.

For a fixed stratified design and a stated bounded group-CATE model, Theorem 2.1 optimizes a linear combination of observed group estimators; that fixed-design linear-estimator problem and the present joint design--all-estimator problem are non-nested.
The Gram--Schmidt Walk design controls a covariance-based balance--robustness trade-off and yields MSE and asymptotic inference guarantees for Horvitz--Thompson estimation.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.
Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.
Exact binary ATE intervals under balanced Bernoulli or matched-pair assignment can be computed with \(O(\log n)\) randomization tests.
Exact conservative stratified binary ATE inference can be obtained by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over compatible potential-outcome tables.

body.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-specified sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction gives an exact finite conic game and dual certificate for the invariant optimal-design correspondence; a rational \(J=2,s=1\) instance rules out every paired--Bernoulli mixture. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while at and above the threshold the leading term leaves a measure-valued face. Exact selection on that face remains open. At \(\rho=1/2\), the concrete residual problem uses \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\), \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\), and the scale \(J^{4/3}\{R_J-1/(2J)\}\); the candidate hard-budget term is upper-bound evidence, not an established epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.

project_justification.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 solves the unrestricted binary fixed-population experiment, while Hull2026BoundedOutcomes solves an unrestricted bounded-interval problem whose endpoint-valued schedules contain the present binary endpoint as a strict subclass. Hull's value and procedure transfer only through an endpoint least-favourable-prior lower bound and a uniform upper-bound sandwich, not by class identity. Bai2022MatchedPairs studies a superpopulation stratified half-treatment criterion, and deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage studies linear estimation under a fixed stratified design; both are non-nested with the present joint fixed-population design--estimator problem. None characterizes exact-minimizer limits on the measure-valued first-order face under a latent armwise discordance budget.
project_justification.niche: The sensitivity restriction breaks full unit exchangeability without treating unobserved potential-outcome discordance as pretreatment information. It leaves a finite but nontransitive observation experiment in which correlated assignment laws and nonlinear posterior-mean estimators can be jointly optimal.
project_justification.fill: For each selected \(s\), the project supplies the normalized assignment-marked orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk sensitivity frontier, a first-order measure face, and exact randomization-test inversion. It isolates rather than claims the unresolved second-order selection theorem: at the critical boundary the candidate residual is an unrestricted Airy/local-experiment functional plus \(\kappa(2\int m\,d\mu-1)\), pending a matching lower expansion and exact-minimizer recovery.

body.related_work: Bai2023WhyRandomize supplies a symmetry template for group averaging, and Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured minimax design may require mixed assignment strategies under a difference-in-means precision criterion. At \(s=J\), \(\Theta_{J,J}\) is exactly the unrestricted binary schedule class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026, so Proposition 2 is an exact reduction to that experiment. By contrast, \(\Theta_{J,J}\) is only the endpoint-valued subclass of Hull2026BoundedOutcomes's bounded-interval class. Hull's common minimax value and Bernoulli/nonlinear procedure transfer to the binary subclass by sandwiching: the endpoint-supported least-favourable prior supplies the lower bound, while Hull's uniform bounded-class risk bound supplies the upper bound. No class identity or experiment equivalence is asserted. Bai2022MatchedPairs considers a superpopulation stratified half-treatment problem, whereas deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage fixes the stratified design and optimizes within a linear estimator class. Those two problems are non-nested with the present fixed-array problem, which jointly optimizes every ex ante assignment law and every measurable clipped estimator under latent armwise pair discordance. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 and AronowLopatto2026 inform balance and design-unbiasedness comparisons, and Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 inform exact inversion. The Airy expansion in SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 motivates the \(J^{-4/3}\) residual scale but does not supply a measure-valued pair-orbit epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact orbit kernel and conic contact system are finite and computable for every \(J\), and the rational \(J=2,s=1\) certificate proves strict noncanonicality. Numerical enumeration for \(J=2,3,4\) is only an early-kill check: critical grids have materially different coordinate ranges and do not determine a limiting exact-minimizer face. The second-order bookkeeping now isolates \(\Delta_J=s_J-J/2\) and \(\kappa_J=\Delta_J/J^{2/3}\). If a design correction is \((2\bar m_J-1)\Delta_J/J^2\), multiplying by \(J^{4/3}\) gives \(\kappa_J(2\bar m_J-1)\), exactly the scale of the unrestricted Airy correction. This is candidate upper-bound evidence only. No matching lower expansion, equicoercivity theorem, or exact-minimizer recovery has been proved. Finite \(\kappa\), \(\kappa=+\infty\), \(\kappa=-\infty\), and \(\rho>1/2\) require separate analyses. The van Trees applications in Theorems 4 and 5 use smooth boundary-vanishing priors and positive finite-cell experiments, so the tightened score, differentiation, boundary-flux, and positive-definiteness conditions remain satisfied.
body.honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not a quantity learned from observed outcomes. Every risk, optimal face, asymptotic regime, and confidence set is conditional on the selected value or sequence. At \(s=0\), paired assignment yields exact recovery. At \(s=J\), the schedule class is exactly the unrestricted binary class of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026. It is not Hull2026BoundedOutcomes's full bounded-interval class; only the same value and procedure transfer by the endpoint-prior/uniform-upper-bound sandwich. The exact finite orbit representation, endpoint reductions, rational noncanonical separation, first-order value, low-sensitivity concentration, high-sensitivity first-order envelope, and exact inversion are theorem obligations. The complete limit set of exact finite minimizers for \(\rho\ge1/2\) remains open, and the stated Airy-plus-budget functional is not claimed as a proved epi- or \(\Gamma\)-limit.
